questions.stem: Two batch jobs on G1 each allocate 20 GB over an hour. Job A parses each record and drops it at once. Job B parses the same records into a buffer of 500,000 and drops them when the buffer is written out. Which job spends more time in GC pauses?

options.text: Job B, since its records outlive young collections and get copied into the old generation
options.says: a young collection copies what is alive, so records that outlive a few collections cost copying, promotion and old-generation marking

options.text: About the same, since a young collection costs in proportion to the bytes allocated
options.says: a young collection never visits dead objects; with the same allocation, 2 MB surviving cost 12-13 ms in total and 200 MB surviving cost 508-1251 ms

options.text: Job A, since its collections find more dead records, and finding and freeing them is the work
options.says: dead young objects are not visited at all: their regions are reused whole, so garbage is the cheap part

options.text: About the same, since G1 resizes its young generation to keep each pause near its target
options.says: with the same allocation and heap, G1's pause count and total grew several times over when objects lived longer

origin.section: A Young Collection Costs What Survives, Not What Was Allocated

questions.stem: A team on Java 21 moves a service from G1 to ZGC with -XX:+UseZGC, keeping its 1 GB heap, which is mostly a long-lived cache. Every Pause line in the new GC log is under 0.1 ms, yet the p99 latency is worse than before. What explains it?

options.text: Not the collector, since pauses under 0.1 ms are too short to move a p99 latency
options.says: a thread that allocates while the heap is full waits for the cycle to free memory, and that wait is not a Pause line

options.text: Not the collector, since ZGC marks and moves objects on its own threads, beside the requests
options.says: when the heap fills before a cycle ends, the request thread itself stops in an allocation stall

options.text: The collector, since a request thread waits for free memory when the heap fills before a cycle ends
options.says: single-generation ZGC marks the whole heap each cycle; when allocation outruns it, the log shows Allocation Stall lines, about 20 ms each in the page's run

options.text: The collector, since its many short pauses add up to more stopped time than G1's longer ones
options.says: the short pauses added up to about 1 ms per run; the waiting happened in stalls, not pauses

origin.section: Each Collector Puts the Cost Somewhere: Pauses, Stalls or CPU

questions.stem: A test drops its last reference to a key, calls System.gc() once, waits on a reference queue until the key's own WeakReference is enqueued (giving up after 5 s), then asserts that a WeakHashMap holding that key is empty. It passes on laptops and times out on the CI agents, whose JVM options add -XX:+DisableExplicitGC. What does that flag do to the test?

options.text: The flag limits the call to a young collection, which leaves a key that has reached the old generation
options.says: with the flag set the call starts no collection of any kind, young or full

options.text: The flag makes the call return at once, and no collection runs that could find the key unreachable
options.says: -XX:+DisableExplicitGC turns System.gc() into a no-op; the page's run returned after 0 ms with the weak reference not cleared

options.text: The flag makes the call return at once, and the collection runs in the background after the test gives up
options.says: with this flag the call starts no collection, in the background or otherwise; the page's run returned after 0 ms with the weak reference still set. A concurrent cycle comes from -XX:+ExplicitGCInvokesConcurrent, and the caller waits for it

options.text: The flag limits the call to clearing references, but the map drops its entries only when it next grows
options.says: with the flag set the call does nothing, so no reference is cleared; and the map removes entries for queued references on its next call, such as size()

origin.section: System.gc() Is a Request, and JVM Flags Decide What It Does

questions.stem: A thumbnail service on G1 keeps 2,000 thumbnails as SoftReferences, in a heap otherwise near its limit. A burst of traffic needs room for a few more thumbnails than is free. What happens to the cache?

options.text: A few of the oldest go, since the collector frees about as much as the new allocation needs
options.says: in the page's run none of the 10 entries was left once 12 MB more had been allocated; a collection that can't make room clears every soft reference

options.text: None of them go yet, since soft references wait for a full collection such as System.gc() to clear them
options.says: a full System.gc() kept all 10 entries in the page's run; they were cleared when an allocation needed the memory

options.text: A few of the least recently read go, since the collector keeps the soft references used most lately
options.says: HotSpot keeps recently read soft references longer only while the heap has room; near the limit it clears them all

options.text: Nearly all of them go at once, since the collector clears soft references together when an allocation needs room
options.says: a full System.gc() with room kept all 10 entries, but once memory was short a collection cleared all 10 together

origin.section: A Soft Cache Survives Collections While There Is Room, and Empties When an Allocation Doesn't Fit
